source.title: MEOW: MEMOry Supervised LLM Unlearning Via Inverted Facts
source.authors: Tianle Gu; Kexin Huang; Ruilin Luo; Yuanqi Yao; Yujiu Yang; Yan Teng; Yingchun Wang

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; some equations and figures have extraction/OCR formatting issues, but the reported table values used here are legible.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates unlearning quality and utility with its own benchmark metric, but does not test whether attacks recover forgotten knowledge.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ToFU forget-quality and model-utility results, but no fine-tuning recovery attack, activation ablation, quantization, or prompting-only recovery test. Its MEMO values are used to select inverted facts and are not attack results. The paper also describes MEOW as robust against extraction, but supplies no extraction-attack outcome.
record.test_reason: The study proposes MEOW, a new unlearning method, and reports ToFU forget quality and model utility, plus NLU/NLG ability. Forget quality is a p-value for similarity to a retain model that never saw the forgotten authors. These results bear on A's 'forgets while keeping general ability' component, measured differently from the originals' chance-accuracy metric. No recovery attack of any kind is run, so A's 'attacks don't recover it' part and versions B–F are untested. The robustness claim for MEOW is asserted only.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that MEOW clearly improves ToFU forget quality over existing methods, keeps model utility without notable decline, and slightly improves NLU on some benchmarks. They acknowledge a slight utility drop, possible added hallucination and hyperparameter sensitivity. The claim that the unlearned model resists extraction appears only as an introductory assertion, with no supporting experiment.
record.recipe_differences: MEOW generates inverted facts, ranks them using MEMO, and fine-tunes on selected facts. It is not a recovery attack; the paper also compares established unlearning baselines. The reported results do not test the claim's attack recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that forget quality varies with the number of inverted facts and whether the highest- or lowest-MEMO facts are selected; model utility falls as more inverted facts are used. It also reports hyperparameter sensitivity for baselines.
record.problems: No recovery or extraction attacks are run, despite the paper's robustness assertion. Forget quality is a p-value for similarity to a retain model rather than direct target-knowledge accuracy; the paper does not establish chance-level performance. LLaMA2 baseline results in the ToFU comparison are stated to come from Ji et al. (2024), rather than being reproduced here.
record.rows_left_out: No recovery-attack results are reported. Baseline-method values and NLU/NLG benchmark metrics are not included in rows because they do not test recovery of the targeted knowledge; LLaMA2 baseline values in Table 1 are adopted from Ji et al. (2024).

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the forgotten knowledge. Targeted-knowledge accuracy versus chance is not reported directly. No hazardous-knowledge benchmark such as WMDP is used.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack.
No activation ablation, and no analysis of whether knowledge is blocked or deleted.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery test.
MEOW is said to prevent extraction after open-sourcing, but no attack is run against it.

missing.what: MEOW NLU/NLG on Llama2 ToFU-5%: PIQA 0.6477 vs 0.6235, ARC-E 0.7789 vs 0.7702, ARC-C 0.5585 vs 0.5719, small MAUVE/BLEU changes. Bears directly on A's 'keeps general ability'. rows_left_out excluded these on the wrong ground.
Ablation of MEMO selection versus random selection on Llama2: F.Q. 0.7559→0.99 (1%), 0.7126→0.8655 (5%), 0.5909→0.6323 (10%).
Sensitivity to the number of inverted facts (1–7) and the H/L selection strategy: utility falls monotonically, F.Q. varies by model and strategy.
F.Q. and M.U. over unlearning steps on ToFU-5% Llama2. MEOW's F.Q. rises to a peak at 150 steps, while most baselines collapse after 100 steps.

record.verdict_notes: This is a method paper with no recovery attacks. It cannot speak to shallow unlearning proper, only to A's surface forgetting-plus-utility component. Table 1 reports MEOW at its best-F.Q. checkpoint, and the Llama2 baseline values are copied from Ji et al. (2024). MEOW does 'soft unlearning' by training in false answers (e.g. 'exclusively a playwright'), so forgetting means replacing facts with false ones, not abstaining. Forget quality is a p-value for similarity to the retain model, not accuracy at chance.

versions.untested_parts: The paper evaluates benchmark forget quality and model utility, but does not directly measure targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance and does not test whether simple attacks recover knowledge.
No small-set fine-tuning recovery attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or access-versus-deletion analysis is tested.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual, or in-context recovery test is reported.
MEOW is described as robust, but resistance to the specified attacks is not evaluated.

source_check.notes: MEOW hyperparameters are tuned per model and split (Table 5: 2–6 new facts, H vs L selection, 37–311 steps). The Table 2 step was chosen for highest F.Q., the evaluation metric itself. Table 2 NLU/NLG results (Llama2 ToFU-5%) are not rows: PIQA 0.6477 vs 0.6235, ARC-E 0.7789 vs 0.7702, ARC-C 0.5585 vs 0.5719. Robustness to extraction is only asserted, never tested.

statements.correction: MEOW, LLaMA2-7B-Chat, ToFU-1%: F.Q. 0.99 vs origin 0.00 (retain 1.00); F.Q. is a KS p-value against the retain model, not accuracy; no attacks tested. M.U. 0.54 vs 0.62 for both origin and retain models (Table 1). NLU/NLG roughly preserved on ToFU-5% (Table 2).
statements.problem: Cites r2 (MEOW, F.Q. only) for 'removed to retrain or gold level while utility is kept'. The statement gives no MEOW numbers and leaves the study out of its 'why' list. The forgetting part fits, but MEOW's ToFU utility falls below both the origin and retain models, so 'utility is kept' overstates this study. The catalog's own verdict l1 marks utility as limits_scope.

The cited rows (r2, r10) are MEOW's Llama2 F.Q. values, 0.99 at 1% and 0.63 at 10%. The statement's TOFU sentence names this study's models, but MEOW does not have 1% F.Q. at or below 0.01, and its utility does not collapse at 5%/10%. The only size dependence the cited rows show is F.Q. falling as the forget set grows, which the statement does not say. Even the paper's Llama2 baselines at 1% have F.Q. 0.25–0.66, not ≤0.01.
